questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic opportunities but also places where I could travel.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was actually pretty easy to get the information from UCPH before arriving in Australia. Søren, the exchange coordinator, was so helpful and made it easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any from UCPH, as it was not required. We had an incident on campus during the semester, where UCPH contacted me to secure if I was okay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The exchange students get guaranteed housing on campus. You simply apply for these through the website

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: As a post-grad, I did not get to choose meal plans. But there were kitchens

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is expensive and they have a lot of fees. You are also required to buy all your pots and pans yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply for courses through ISIS (there website), but you get answers of registration a week before study start. This makes it hard to know your schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student central and every college have their own student help desk

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 4/4 courses but ended up switching one course

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose the courses they find interesting, then show up in the first week and figure out whether you want to continue on the course. Otherwise, you have two weeks to change the course

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was okay. I took three of the toughest courses within the College of Business and Economics. But the level of courses in general varies within the different colleges

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think that UCPH is more theoretical in addition to many other universities. ANU was more applied, which was also tough, since you are not used to think in the same directions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Valuation
Applied Corporate Finance
Portfolio Construction
Trading & Markets

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. Trading & Markets is one of the best courses that I have ever had. They had readings for every week and pre-recorded lectures, then you show up to an in-person lecture to discuss what the pre-recorded lecture was about. In the tutorials they built a trading platform, where you used the theory in practice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cleaning fees, buying equipment for the room. Basically, everything that had to do with housing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer, was expensive. Meat also expensive. The coffee is great everywhere in Australia, and only 5 dollars (approx. 25 DKK)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything. Every Village on campus played against each other in different types of sports. There were also the Sports club for the University. A lot of parties, and different creative clubs were available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports. They gave you the opportunity to be social.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Tasmania, Melbourne and Sydney. Sydney is only 3 hours in a bus away. Fly Jetstar, as this is cheap. Many took the bus from Canberra to Melbourne, which is 8 hours. But the flight takes 50 minutes and is only 20 dollars more expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. As the Australian and danish culture is more or less the same.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live on campus. I chose Yukeembruk Village. Even though it was expensive I had a lovely time there. You felt welcome from day one and they host social get togethers every Thursday.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Australian people are so kind

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the kindness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Enjoy ANU. Canberra is not known to anyone, but it is a great city. I loved every bit of it. ANU is one of the best universities in Australia. I met a lot of Australians, and they told me that people on exchange want to study in Sydney or Melbourne, because they are large city, but the students in Australia actually want to study at ANU.

2) Socialise. The time in Canberra will be so much better with friends.

3) Travel around. Canberra is close to the east-coast. Visit some cities, go on surf camp and enjoy that you do not have the same winter down under as we have here

4) Remember sun-screen. The sun is dangerous.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not be afraid to ask questions. The employees in the student central are nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academics and making friends worldwide.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going far away from home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
